hypothesis_tested: Both RS execution profiles (minimal and dialogic) forbid appending advice AND a new question/probe. Permitting a brief warm close or one open question (while still forbidding advice, to preserve the family's identity) should recover quality lost to this constraint.
hypothesis_correction_before_testing: The initial narrower hypothesis (minimal profile specifically is the problem) was checked and disconfirmed before building any fix: dialogic actually lost to baseline WORSE (21/21=100%) than minimal (11/13=84.6%), because both profiles share the same no-question/no-advice constraint.
method: Regenerated the 31 Restatement-family routed replies (300l's external test) with only the RS guidance text swapped to the warm-close variant (308l) -- MS candidate, seed, dialogue, requested_action_id held byte-identical. Re-ran the same blind pairwise quality instrument (305l/306l pattern) comparing the new replies against the SAME original baseline replies.
interpretation: Real, meaningful, but partial quality improvement -- traded for a real, meaningful risk increase, not a clean win. Baseline win rate dropped 19.4 points (93.5% -> 74.2%), and a genuine EQUIVALENT verdict appeared for the first time (0/31 before, 5/31 after) -- the hypothesis was directionally correct and the fix has real quality effect, not noise. But it does not flip the overall conclusion: baseline still wins a clear majority (74.2%). Two compounding causes visible in remaining-loss judge rationales: (1) the warm-close instruction is not followed 100% of the time by this weak 8B generator, consistent with the ~65% RS content-following rate independently verified earlier this session; (2) even when added, some replies anchor their restatement to OLDER conversation content rather than the latest turn. CRITICAL ADDITION (user-flagged fairness gap, closed by 313l/314l): risk was NOT re-measured in the first pass of this round on the unverified assumption it was unaffected. Re-measuring with the exact same instrument shows risk more than DOUBLED (mean 0.29 -> 0.61, nonzero items 6/31 -> 12/31), almost entirely from the model inventing specific unsupported personal details (e.g. 'financial pressure', 'this new job', 'parents apologizing for being strict' -- none present in the actual conversation) once given more generative freedom to add a warm close. This is the real cost side of the quality gain, and it was invisible until the same measurement standard was applied to both conditions.
conclusion_vs_original_claim: Still does not support the original claim that PM (RS+MS) matches or beats baseline on quality, and the warm-close fix is not a straightforward improvement to adopt -- it partially recovers quality at the cost of more than doubling hallucination-type risk. The quality problem is real but not fundamental to RS/MS's mechanism (fixable in degree through card-content design), but this particular fix has its own real downside that a quality-only re-measurement would have missed entirely. Any future iteration must measure quality AND risk together, not sequentially with assumptions substituting for the untested dimension.
next_scientific_action: Per explicit user direction, MP rule-based Step1 rescue is the next concrete work item. Any further RS quality work (recency-anchoring fix, stronger generator retest, broader family rebalancing) requires a separate user decision -- not pursued further in this round.
